clue.text: Louis maybe following Tom, Dick and Harry

parts.note: Joe Louis was the world heavyweight boxing champion, so Louis is an example of a Joe
a following is a body of supporters, one's public

explanation.surface: Someone called Louis trails behind a trio of ordinary men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Louis maybe' looks like a king of France; it is the boxer Joe Louis, standing for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Every Tom, Dick and Harry means any ordinary person, the typical citizen, which is what the phrase names.

clue.text: Give lift to funny fellow young Pike, perhaps

parts.note: to jack up a car is to give it a lift
an odd fish or queer fish is a strange person

explanation.surface: Someone offers a ride to a comic, perhaps a youngster named Pike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pike' is capitalised to look like a person's surname; it is the freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is a young pike, and the fuller name for the fish is used the same way, so pike is one example.

clue.text: Members of Parliament about to send messages quickly?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the picked run is read backwards
members are parts, so some consecutive letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: MPs are on the point of firing off some quick notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members of Parliament' reads as MPs; instead 'Members of' takes LIAME from inside 'Parliament', and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail lets someone dispatch a message almost instantly, hence the question mark on quickly.

clue.text: Free French articles second poor writer penned

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the articles are written round the other pieces

parts.note: un and le are the French indefinite and definite articles
a hack is a mediocre writer who churns out copy

explanation.surface: Some French grammar words and a second-rate writer get locked up, then released.
explanation.definitionFit: To unshackle someone is to release them from chains, which is to set them at liberty.

clue.text: Romance is over after trouble crops up

indicators.note: after says the words before it come later in the answer
in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
on can mean over, as in a lecture on a subject

explanation.surface: A love affair finishes once some problem appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crops up' reverses the word for trouble; 'after' says that turned piece leads, though the clue prints it last. 'over' meaning on is as in a talk on a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a love affair, often a secret one, so it is a romance.

clue.text: Give false alarm to keen seducer of women

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to cry
a wolf is a man who pursues women

explanation.surface: Someone warns a lothario off with a phoney alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager; here it is the verb to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: From the fable of the shepherd boy, to cry wolf is to raise an alarm that proves baseless.

clue.text: For example, short note giving permission

parts.note: say is used to introduce an instance, as for example is

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter of the note is dropped

parts.note: soh is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A brief memo granting leave, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims SOH to SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone has your say-so means they have your authorisation.

clue.text: Cold meal somewhere in US served up half-heartedly

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards
the heart of the word is its double L, and half of that pair is removed

parts.note: Dallas is a city in Texas

explanation.surface: A cold plate dished out without enthusiasm somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' cuts DALLAS to DALAS, and 'served up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad of raw vegetables or cold meats is a typical cold dish for lunch.

clue.text: It's called weightlifting, in the main

definitions.text: It's called weightlifting, in the main

parts.words: It's called weightlifting, in the main
parts.note: the main is the open sea, and the weight lifted is a ship's anchor, hauled up by sailors chanting as they pull

explanation.surface: A description of a gym exercise, in general terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly'; it means on the high seas, where sailors shout this chant while heaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors sang the call as they hauled ropes or raised the anchor together, a literal lifting of weight at sea.

clue.text: Author associated famously with soldiers

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to get on famously is to get on very well

explanation.surface: A writer best known for his links with the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'famously' looks like an adverb about fame; it is the informal 'very well'.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell wrote Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Excellence of a sort

definitions.meaning: ... is high quality, as in a player with real ...

explanation.definitionFit: Class means both superior quality and a category of things.

clue.text: Move on lady who is drunk and disorderly

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order, like a drunk told to move on

explanation.surface: Telling a tipsy rowdy woman to move along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move on' reads as a police order to the reveller; 'Move' rearranges ON LADY WHO, and the closing phrase describes the messy result.
explanation.definitionFit: Done any old how means sloppily and without order, the state of a staggering reveller.

clue.text: Peasants with iron will, arguably, recalled

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: shall and will are often used interchangeably, a point grammarians argue over

explanation.surface: Peasants with a steely determination are summoned back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns SHALL into LLAHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellahs are agricultural labourers in Arab countries, so they are farm workers of the poorest class.

clue.text: Unusual line Labour Party's taken about Democrat, doing Uturn

indicators.note: a U-turn goes back the way it came, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: Lab is the usual abbreviation for the British Labour Party
do is the verb behind doing, as in what to do

explanation.surface: A political party performs one more embarrassing about-turn on its policy.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator turns the whole string, which reads backwards as the answer; 'taken about' only joins the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddball as an adjective means peculiar or eccentric, which is strange.

clue.text: Pin, for girl, might be a small Christmas gift

definitions.text: Pin, for girl, might be a small Christmas gift

parts.words: Pin, for girl, might be a small Christmas gift
parts.note: pins is slang for legs, and a girl's leg is what fills a hosiery item; it is also the little present in a hung-up Christmas sock

explanation.surface: A hair pin or brooch would make a nice little Christmas present for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin' looks like a brooch or hairpin; it is slang for a leg, which fills a stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A small present put into a hung-up Christmas sock is the usual name for a cheap little gift.

clue.text: Strike oil and try new ploy to get market control few enjoy

indicators.note: strike as in strike down; the word is knocked into a new order

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: new means remade, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm that strikes oil and tries a fresh tactic dominates the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike oil' sounds like a lucky find, but 'Strike' and 'new' each scramble only the word beside them, and 'try' sits between them unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligopoly is a market dominated by a small number of suppliers, the Greek root oligo meaning few.

clue.text: Famous match in series having finish that's fairly even

parts.note: a leg is one game of a series, as in the first leg of a tie
the end is the finish

indicators.note: even means the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A celebrated contest in a series ends in a fairly balanced finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fairly even' looks like 'quite level'; it takes the even letters of 'fairly', A, R and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary figure is so well known as to be the stuff of legend, so very well known.

clue.text: Colt once found here by boss — fine revolver, perhaps

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a revolver is one type of firearm, or arm

explanation.surface: A Colt pistol was once found here beside the boss, a fine handgun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' and 'revolver' suggest the gun maker; Colt is a young horse, born on a horse farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A colt is a young male horse, and horses are bred on a breeding farm for horses.

clue.text: He sought vet with pig about to die

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A man looked for a vet because his pig was about to die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to die' reads as one phrase; 'about' is the anagram signal for HE SOUGHT VET and PIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up the ghost is an idiom meaning to expire, from the spirit leaving the body.

clue.text: Umpire excited about maiden of highest quality

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the M
excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire gets worked up over a maiden over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' turns UMPIRE into PREIUM, which goes 'about' M.
explanation.definitionFit: Premium as an adjective means superior, first-class, as with premium goods.

clue.text: Lots found drug-taking repellent

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the drug goes inside the word for lots

parts.note: a hatful is a large quantity, lots
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Many people find taking drugs disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug-taking' reads as one word; HATFUL is 'taking' the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hateful arouses loathing, so it is repugnant.

clue.text: Good — Lear's daughter's upset about being a tormentor

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed name surrounds the G
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: One of King Lear's daughters is distressed at becoming his persecutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns REGAN into NAGER, which goes 'about' G.
explanation.definitionFit: A nagger pesters someone constantly, harassing them with complaints.

clue.text: Missionary given drink, after being taken in

indicators.note: the word for after is taken inside the drink

parts.note: ale is beer
post means after, as in postwar

explanation.surface: A missionary accepts a drink after being welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like 'deceived'; it means the word for after goes inside the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is one sent out to spread the faith, as the twelve disciples were.

clue.text: Leave food container outside, making cat cross

indicators.note: the container is placed outside the word for leave

parts.note: a tin is a can for food
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Leaving the food tin outside makes the cat angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry'; it means a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the hybrid offspring of a male tiger and a lioness.

clue.text: Man's diet? Want lady forgetting a wobble!

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out, so the letter a is not part of the result
a wobble shakes things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letter a, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man on a diet longs for a woman and loses his resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, and a diet is a parliament. Rearrange WANT LADY without one A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tynwald is the parliament of the Isle of Man, and diet is an old word for a legislative assembly.

clue.text: Leading character's sound as a bell in The Coral Island

parts.note: A is the first letter of the alphabet
to toll is to ring, as a bell does

explanation.surface: The hero of a novel rings out as clear as a bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Coral Island' is a Victorian adventure novel, and 'Leading character' suggests its hero; it is A, first of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped reef of coral enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Oath given surprisingly just before kind of trial

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: good means righteous, just
grief is a trial in the sense of a painful affliction

explanation.surface: Someone swears in surprise just before a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' suggests a court; it means an ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of astonishment, a mild expletive uttered when surprised.

clue.text: Scent a drifter, say, is following

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a roamer is someone who wanders without settling

explanation.surface: A vagrant leaves a smell behind.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'a roamer' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive smell, usually a pleasant one.

clue.text: Fish about for some material

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for fish to get some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is an artificial silk fibre, so a fabric.

clue.text: On reflection, it appears the same Indian language

indicators.text: On reflection, it appears the same
indicators.note: the answer reads the same backwards as forwards, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, this Indian tongue looks identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Malayalam is the Dravidian tongue of Kerala in south-west India.
